chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu al-Subbah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who sends money to a land, he said: The one who wants to send it with him said, 'Lend it to me, and I will repay you when you arrive in the land.' He said, 'There is no objection to this.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no objection/It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to borrow money for travel expenses with a promise to repay upon the lender's arrival?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates a specific commercial arrangement where a traveler lends money to a local who promises repayment upon the lender's return, highlighting the flexibility of *qard* (interest-free loan) in pre-modern trade logistics. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on the validity of mutual consent (*taradi*) in financial contracts, provided no riba (usury) is involved, and reflects the practical needs of merchants in the Abbasid era. The permissibility here serves as a foundational precedent for modern Islamic banking concepts of deferred repayment and cross-regional liquidity management.
